conviction_note: Balanced evidence: the mid-quarter raise of 8 Sep put consensus on top of a guide set with three weeks of the quarter left, so the reported quarter is close to pre-announced (consensus revenue $705.2m against guide ~$705m). The stock trades on the Q4 guide and member adds, and the skew already leans the way my small negatives point. I put p_up at 49 on a big move (11.5%, between the 10.1% event-implied move and the 13.6% median reaction). That gives -0.23. The findings sum to -0.5, and the two measures agree in sign.
bar: Q3 2026 revenue of about $705m and adjusted EBITDA of $117-120m, the company guide raised on 2026-09-08 (https://www.chime.com/newsroom/chime-announces-agreement-to-acquire-stride-bank/). This replaced the 5 Aug guide of $680-690m revenue and $105-110m EBITDA (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001795586/000179558626000046/ex991q226.htm). Consensus is $705.2m revenue and $0.09 EPS, with a whisper of $0.15 (Earnings Whispers via Finviz, 2026-10-27, https://finviz.com/news/409422/chimes-stride-bank-deal-lifts-the-bar-as-prime-and-instant-loans-face-a-proof-quarter). Another Earnings Whispers page shows a stale $0.06 EPS and $678m revenue (https://www.earningswhispers.com/epsdetails/CHYM). Revenue bar: guide and consensus agree. EPS bar: disputed ($0.06 vs $0.09) and affected by $16-20m of Q3 restructuring cash charges. Implied Q4 from the FY guide of $2.76-2.77bn: about $738-748m.
positioning_check: Short interest 25.93M shares with 3.5 days to cover at the 2026-09-30 settlement (https://massive.com/quote/chym). That is up from 23.1M and 4.2 days at 2026-07-31 (curvedtrading, snippet only; the page returned 403) and was about 6.1% of float in August (equibles, snippet only, https://equibles.com/stocks/chym/shortinterest). Not crowded. Borrow fee about 0.3% (curvedtrading snippet). Baseline: 25-delta skew +10.65 vol points (downside paid), put/call OI 1.08, ATM IV 72.4%, event-implied move 10.13%. Into the print the stock is +4.86% over 5 days and +8.13% over 20 days, and 12.6% below its 52-week high. In October Deutsche Bank upgraded to Buy (PT $35) and Seaport raised its PT to $42, so the sell-side is leaning long into a put-rich chain.

findings.finding: On 2026-09-08, with about three weeks of the quarter left, Chime raised Q3 guidance to about $705m revenue (~30% YoY) and $117-120m adjusted EBITDA, from $680-690m and $105-110m. Consensus moved onto it: $705.2m revenue and $0.09 EPS, with a $0.15 whisper. In Q2 the company beat the top of its guide by about 4% ($670m against $633-643m), but that guide was set a full quarter ahead. A guide set with three weeks left leaves much less room, so the revenue beat is likely around 1% and the whisper sets a high bar for EPS.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 (5 Aug): beat the top of guide by about 4% and raised FY, +20.56%. Q1 2026 (6 May): EPS $0.13 against $0.03 consensus and a FY raise, but the stock fell 12.52% on a cautious outlook and Chime Prime margin worries. Q3 2025: -5.39% despite a raise. The stock trades on the outlook, not on the size of the beat.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: consensus sits on the guide and the stock rose 5.9% on the raise day. What is not visible is how small the revenue beat can be once the bar was reset mid-quarter. If the market fully saw that, the whisper would sit nearer consensus and the stock would not have run up 8% in the 20 days before the print.
findings.independence: Consensus and whisper are from Earnings Whispers via Finviz, 2026-10-27 (https://finviz.com/news/409422/chimes-stride-bank-deal-lifts-the-bar-as-prime-and-instant-loans-face-a-proof-quarter). The Q2 beat history is from the Q2 release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001795586/000179558626000046/ex991q226.htm) and the Q1 release's Q2 guide of $633-643m (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001795586/000179558626000035/ex991q126.htm).

findings.finding: Q3 carries $16-20m of net cash restructuring charges from the ~10% workforce cut announced 2026-07-31. A $9-12m reversal of stock compensation partly offsets it, for a net income hit of $6-9m (about $0.02 a share on ~380m shares). This makes the GAAP EPS bar ($0.06-0.09) noisy. Adjusted EBITDA likely excludes the charges.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior restructuring quarter on this name. The stock barely moved when the cut was announced (secondary summaries).
findings.source_date: 2026-08 (10-Q for the quarter ended 2026-06-30, subsequent-events note)
findings.why_not_priced: It is disclosed, so it is largely priced. The risk is a headline GAAP EPS miss against an aggregator EPS that did not net out the charge. If that were fully understood, the two EPS consensus sources would not disagree ($0.06 vs $0.09).
findings.independence: The 8-K of 2026-07-31 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001795586/000179558626000046/chym-20260731.htm) is the same disclosure, so the two count as one source.

findings.finding: Management raised MyPay limits to $1,000 and said loss rates would rise modestly. MyPay's Q2 loss rate was 0.9% and its transaction profit $73m, so a rise in losses could take a little off transaction margin (73% in Q2) in Q3/Q4.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Unknown for this line on its own. Q1 2026's -12.5% was tied to margin worries about Chime Prime, so margin quality has moved this stock.
findings.why_not_priced: The company guided to it, so it sits inside what the market was told and is sized near zero. It only matters if the rise is larger than 'modest'. If the market feared that, the EBITDA guide raise to $117-120m would have been discounted, and it was not.
findings.independence: The Q2 release gives the 0.9% loss rate and $73m transaction profit (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001795586/000179558626000046/ex991q226.htm). No independent read on Q3 losses.

findings.finding: The Bancorp (TBBK) is one of Chime's two partner banks. It reported Q3 2026 card gross dollar volume of $54.3bn, +23.4% YoY and +1.6% QoQ. Chime's own Q2 purchase volume grew 17% (20% including OIT), so partner-bank volume held up through the quarter. It is a proxy: Bancorp's GDV includes many other fintech programmes.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Purchase volume and payments revenue are 64% of revenue ($430m of $670m in Q2). Q2's volume and revenue beat came with +20.6%.
findings.why_not_priced: A counterparty print after Chime last spoke (8 Sep), but the ~30% revenue guide already implies strong volume. If the market had read it as upside, revenue consensus would sit above the $705m point guide rather than on it.
findings.independence: Proxy only. Visa's fiscal Q4 release shows total payments volume +9% (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001403161/000140316126000126/q42026earningsrelease.htm), but I could not extract the US debit figure.

findings.finding: SoFi, the closest listed consumer-fintech peer, reported Q3 2026 in late October: a record 1.2M new members (17.1M total, +35% YoY), deposits +$5.8bn to $51.3bn, adjusted revenue +44%, a raised FY guide and a 2027 outlook. That supports the read of a healthy consumer-fintech acquisition environment going into Chime's Q3, a seasonally strong quarter for member adds against its 1.8M FY net-add target (about 900k needed in H2).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Member adds have mattered: Q1 2026 added ~700k (beat), but the stock fell on the outlook. The 1.8M target, raised from 1.4M in Q2, came with +20.6%.
findings.why_not_priced: Peer read-through is transmission, not Chime's own number. Some of it is in the 20-day run-up of +8%. If fully priced, the put skew would not be +10.65.
findings.independence: Proxy. Chime's 1.8M net-add target comes from the Q2 call summary (https://quartr.com/events/chime-financial-inc-chym-q2-2026_FVlbs8Ga).

findings.finding: Positioning into the print leans long while the options lean short. Deutsche Bank upgraded to Buy on 8 Oct (PT $30 to $35) and Seaport raised its PT to $42. The stock is +8.1% over 20 days and +4.9% over 5. The front-expiry 25-delta skew is +10.65 vol points with put/call OI at 1.08. Short interest is moderate (25.9M shares, 3.5 days to cover), so a squeeze is a weak mechanism. On a stock that has fallen on 3 of its 5 prints, a run-up into an in-line quarter makes a sell-the-news outcome somewhat more likely.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 2026: beat, raise and a run-up gave -12.5% on the outlook. Q2 2026: +20.6% from a lower base. 3 of 5 prints fell.
findings.why_not_priced: The skew itself says this is partly priced: downside is already paid for. The size here is what the run-up and the upgrades add beyond the skew. It stays small because the skew agrees with the sign.
findings.independence: Short interest from https://massive.com/quote/chym (2026-09-30). The October analyst actions come from a search summary (TipRanks/Fly), not fetched.

baseline_tension: My small net negative agrees with the +10.65 put skew and cuts slightly against the +8% 20-day run-up. Where it agrees with the skew it is probably priced, which is why p_up sits at 49 and not lower.
lessons_applied: Rule 3 / two readings of one fact: the draft's '+0.5 mid-quarter raise shows momentum' and '-1.0 the bar is now high, whisper $0.15' both rest on the 8 Sep raise. Merged into one reported-quarter finding at -0.4.
Rule 2: restructuring charges are a one-off below operating income with no path to the guide. Cut from -0.3 to -0.2.
Rule 6: the MyPay loss-rate rise lands inside what management told the market. Cut from -0.3 to -0.2.
Rule 5: Bancorp GDV and the SoFi peer print are proxies. Kept but trimmed (+0.5 to +0.4 and +0.4 to +0.3), with independence saying so.

Rule 7: the positioning negative agrees with the skew and short interest is not crowded. Trimmed from -0.5 to -0.4. abs_move_pct raised 11.0 to 11.5 because a Q4 guide and possibly a first 2027 framing make a guidance move likely.
